entries.test: Public reporting and Starbucks statements establishing whether the inventory experiment was shut down because of its unreliable results would settle this claim.
entries.note: Marcus asserts the causal explanation in his own voice before quoting supporting reporting.

entries.test: Index inclusion decisions, fund mandates, and disclosed holdings following the three IPOs would show whether index funds were compelled to absorb the stocks rapidly.
entries.note: “Not-yet-profitable” is stronger than “have not yet shown themselves to be profitable.” No definite deadline is given for the predicted purchases.

entries.test: Public evidence of customer retrenchment and resulting failures to meet the companies’ long-term projections, followed by their stock-price records, would test the conditional prediction.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies the condition; “eventually” supplies no deadline.
“May” explicitly presents a possibility rather than a firm prediction.

entries.test: Public records of financial rescues justified by systemic importance and declines in broadly held investment portfolios during the predicted AI-related downturn would test this warning.
entries.note: The imperative wording conveys a substantive prediction of financial rescues and investment losses. It gives no deadline.
